question: A construction worker splashes cement powder (calcium hydroxide, pH ~12) in both eyes. He arrives at the primary health centre 10 minutes later. What is the IMMEDIATE first priority in management?

answers.text: Measure visual acuity in both eyes to document baseline before treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Visual acuity measurement is important but must NEVER delay irrigation in an alkali chemical burn. Every minute of continued contact causes deeper penetration and greater tissue damage.

answers.text: Apply a topical anaesthetic drop, then commence continuous irrigation with normal saline for at least 30 minutes, targeting a conjunctival pH of 7.0–7.4

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Copious immediate irrigation is the single most time-critical intervention in chemical ocular burns. Alkalis cause liquefactive necrosis and penetrate deeper than acids — continued alkali contact destroys the anterior segment and even posterior structures. Irrigation with 2 litres of saline (minimum 30 minutes) must begin within seconds of arrival. Check pH with litmus paper; continue until neutral.

answers.text: Refer immediately to a tertiary ophthalmology centre without any local treatment, to avoid causing further harm

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Delay is the greatest harm. Irrigation must begin at the point of first contact and at the primary centre. Only after thorough irrigation and neutralisation should transfer occur.

answers.text: Apply a topical antibiotic ointment to both eyes to prevent infection, then refer

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Antibiotic prophylaxis is a secondary step. Applying ointment before irrigation would trap the alkali against the ocular surface and worsen injury. Irrigation first — everything else second.

overallFeedback.feedback: Rule: IRRIGATE FIRST, always, in any chemical burn. Alkali (cement, lime, lye) is more dangerous than acid because it causes liquefactive necrosis with deep penetration. Never delay irrigation to document VA, photograph, or refer.
Correct. Alkali burns = immediate irrigation, no delays, 2 litres minimum, target pH 7.0–7.4. Alkali > acid severity because liquefactive necrosis penetrates deeply.
